body.title: Configurable Slack digest to stop notification fatigue killing approver adoption
body.body_original: Bill reports that every single expense pings the approver in Slack, and people are muting the channel entirely, which defeats the purpose of the integration. He proposes a daily digest, but with anything over $500 still pinging in real time, as the ideal design. This is an adoption blocker in month one: if approvers mute the channel, approvals stall and the core workflow breaks. The threshold-plus-digest pattern is a concrete, buildable spec rather than a vague complaint, so it is low-risk to scope.

body.title: Auto-calculate mileage from start/end address to curb inflated reimbursements
body.body_original: Today employees type mileage distance by hand, and Bill notes the numbers are 'creative', i.e. people are inflating distances and finance is eating fraudulent or inaccurate reimbursements. He wants the distance computed automatically from a start and end address. The underlying job is finance control and accuracy, not convenience; this is a compliance and cost-leakage lever, which is why he says finance would 'love you.' Pitching it as a controls feature could strengthen the finance champion relationship on this account.

body.title: Entity-level permissions block a 300-seat EU rollout
body.body_original: Globex runs four legal entities, two in the EU, and today spend is visible across all of them. Their German works council will not accept cross-entity visibility, so finance users and approvers in Germany must be scoped to their own entity's spend only. This is a hard gate: the entire EU rollout of roughly 300 seats is blocked until it ships. Given the labour-council requirement, this is a compliance-driven blocker, not a nice-to-have, and it directly gates expansion revenue.

sources.title: Mobile receipt preview in approval notification is the lever on their month-end close
sources.excerpt: Acme's regional managers approve expenses from their phones, but the approval screen shows only a total with no way to see the receipt image without opening a laptop, so they defer approvals until Monday. Jordan believes showing the receipt image directly in the approval notification would cut two days off close. This is the exact metric his CFO is judging the account on, so this single capability carries the ROI case tied to their March renewal. Solving it would also convert twelve regional managers into daily mobile approvers, deepening adoption and retention.

What is blocking the Globex rollout?.answer: The Globex EU rollout of roughly 300 seats is blocked by entity-level permissions: their German works council will not accept cross-entity spend visibility, so finance users and approvers in Germany must be scoped to only their own entity's spend [1][2]. This is a compliance-driven hard gate tied to the labour-council requirement, and it gates expansion revenue until it ships [1].

sources.title: Entity-level permissions block a 300-seat EU rollout
sources.excerpt: Globex runs four legal entities, two in the EU, and today spend is visible across all of them. Their German works council will not accept cross-entity visibility, so finance users and approvers in Germany must be scoped to their own entity's spend only. This is a hard gate: the entire EU rollout of roughly 300 seats is blocked until it ships. Given the labour-council requirement, this is a compliance-driven blocker, not a nice-to-have, and it directly gates expansion revenue.

What did Initech complain about?.answer: Initech raised three issues: the Slack notifications were too noisy because every expense pinged the approver, causing people to mute the channel [3]; a recurring NetSuite blank-cost-center export bug that has damaged finance's trust [1][2]; and a mileage fraud concern [2].

sources.title: Maya to notify Initech when the NetSuite blank-cost-center export fix ships
sources.excerpt: Maya confirmed the NetSuite export failure is a known bug currently being fixed and committed to telling Initech as soon as the fix ships. This is an explicit commitment on our side tied to a repeat failure that has damaged finance's trust, so closing the loop promptly matters for the relationship. Letting this slip would compound the frustration of a bug that already recurred twice.

sources.title: Initech will run a formal review at the 90-day mark
sources.excerpt: Bill said they'll do a proper review at the ninety-day mark, setting an explicit evaluation checkpoint for the account. This matters because the open items raised on this call, Slack noise, mileage fraud, the NetSuite bug, will likely be judged at that review, making it an informal go/no-go on expansion or continued commitment. We should make sure the digest and NetSuite fix are resolved and the mileage request has a roadmap answer before that date.
